subject: Hermes Analytics: sudden throttling during end-of-month ingest
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@hermesanalytics.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Massive 429s and latency spike during nightly ingest

Hi Lauren,

We started our end-of-month ingest at 02:00 UTC and immediately saw a spike of 429 responses and long tail latencies across our pipelines. Attached are a couple of sample logs — timestamps, request ids, and 20+% error rates for the first 45 minutes. This is impacting downstream reporting and our ops teams are getting paged.

We haven't changed our traffic profile; this is the same pattern we've run for months. Can you look into whether quota/burst rules were changed on your side? We need immediate headroom and a root-cause estimate.

We will be looping in procurement in case we need an emergency capacity add-on.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Data Engineering
Hermes Analytics

Attachments: hermes-429-sample-logs.txt
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: Massive 429s and latency spike during nightly ingest

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding an urgent customer report from Hermes (DEAL-7831). They hit significant 429s during their nightly ingest window starting 02:00 UTC. Attached logs look like token-based 429s plus elevated p99 latencies.

Between us: Hermes is a mid-enterprise committed to a reserved capacity path. This is high visibility — procurement is already on the thread and they're pushing for a quick fix + credits if we caused this. Please advise next steps: temporary headroom, immediate policy rollback, or patch?

I can join an ops call if helpful.

— Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: Massive 429s and latency spike during nightly ingest

Thanks Lauren — looking at logs now. Early hypothesis: a misinterpreted burst window in the recent rate-policy rollout. The change we shipped last week added a per-tenant burst-smoothing step that should have been configured in 1s buckets, but the deployment used a 60s aggregation for some customers behind a feature-flag. Hermes looks like one of the affected tenants — sustained short bursts got aggregated and suppressed, triggering safety valves and severe request shedding.

Plan (short):
- Flip feature flag for Hermes to legacy burst aggregation (immediately).
- Provision temporary headroom on their Dedicated pool for the next 6 hours.
- Push a hotfix to normalize aggregation semantics across all tenants (ETA 3 hours).

I will open a P0 incident and attach the policy diff.

Karthik
Sr. Platform Engineer (Serving Runtime)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: Massive 429s and latency spike during nightly ingest

Appreciate the quick triage. Two asks:
1) Give Hermes immediate bypass capacity and confirm by 10:45 PT so they can re-run the job.
2) Draft a short customer note describing root cause (policy misconfiguration aggregate window), interim mitigations, and our timeline for a full fix and any compensation.

We need a CEO-level summary if this expands beyond Hermes — copy me on updates.

Marissa
VP, Customer Reliability
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@hermesanalytics.com>, Jake Rivers <jake.rivers@hermesanalytics.com>, Procurement <procure@hermesanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: URGENT: Massive 429s and latency spike during nightly ingest

Hi Elena — quick update from our side: we identified a rate-policy aggregation mismatch that caused short bursts to be treated as long sustained load for a subset of customers including Hermes. We've provisioned temporary headroom in your dedicated pool and flipped the feature-flag for your tenant. Can you please re-run the ingest now and confirm whether you still see 429s?

Action items for Hermes: re-run the job and send a short trace if you still see failures.
Action items for us: we will deliver a remediation hotfix within 3 hours and follow up with a formal RCA and any billing adjustments.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact here and will prioritize.

— Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: temporary-headroom-request.txt
From: Elena Park <elena@hermesanalytics.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: URGENT: Massive 429s and latency spike during nightly ingest

Thanks for the fast response team. We re-ran the ingest after the headroom and flag flip and errors dropped to 0.8% within 10 minutes; p99 latency returned to expected range. Appreciate the temporary capacity and the team jumping on this.

Please include the remediation timeline and permanent fix details in the RCA — procurement wants a confirmation we won't see repeat regressions. We'll expect the formal RCA and proposed billing credit for the window of impact.

Elena
Director of Data Engineering
Hermes Analytics
